standards.iec_62233_standard: IEC / EN 62233 Household Appliance EMF Exposure Standard (W <= 1.0 at 30 cm)

pot_sizes.label: Severely Undersized (55% coil coverage, e.g., 10cm cup on 18cm zone)
Slightly Undersized (75% coil coverage, e.g., 14cm pot on 18cm zone)
Exact Match (100% coverage, pan matches coil diameter)
Oversized Pan (125% coverage, base extends past coil ring)

alignments.label: Slightly Off-Center (2-3 cm overhang towards front)
Severely Off-Center (5-6 cm offset, coil perimeter exposed)

materials.name: Heavy Cast Iron / Enamelled Dutch Oven
materials.notes: Optimal ferromagnetic shielding. Magnetic flux lines are tightly trapped within the thick dense base.

materials.name: Tri-Ply Clad Magnetic Stainless Steel (AISI 430 Base)
materials.notes: Standard reference cookware for IEC 62233 compliance testing. High magnetic coupling with moderate fringing.

materials.name: Aluminum Pan with Perforated Ferrous Sandwich Disk
materials.notes: Discontinuous dot-matrix ferrous plate allows significant high-frequency flux to bypass the base into kitchen air.

materials.name: Warped / Concave Deformed Pan Bottom (>2mm air gap)
materials.notes: Air gap between cooktop glass and pan bottom forces magnetic flux lines to spread laterally as intense fringing field.

implants.label: Modern Bipolar Pacemaker / ICD (Close-Spaced Sensing Tip)
Legacy Unipolar Pacemaker (Wide Lead-to-Can Antenna Loop)

burners.label: Front Burner (Direct Edge Proximity, 0 cm offset buffer)
Rear / Back Burner (Physical Counter Depth Clearance, +25 cm buffer)

utensils.label: Solid Stainless Steel Spoon / Metallic Ladle (Conductive)

tiers.name: Negligible Stray Field (Absolute Cardiac Safe)
tiers.icnirp_compliance: Fully Compliant (<8% of 1998 limit, <2% of 2010 limit)
tiers.pacemaker_safety: Absolute Cardiac Safety: Stray field is beneath physiological sensing thresholds for all pacemaker and ICD configurations.
tiers.clinical_verdict: Safe for continuous cooking without distance restrictions.

tiers.name: Compliant Low Field (Domestic Standard)
tiers.icnirp_compliance: Fully Compliant (<32% of 1998 limit, <7.4% of 2010 limit)
tiers.pacemaker_safety: Safe for Modern Bipolar Pacemakers and ICDs. Negligible interference risk at normal standing posture.
tiers.clinical_verdict: Compliant with IEC 62233 household reference levels.

tiers.name: Moderate Fringing Field (Caution for Unipolar Leads)
tiers.icnirp_compliance: Compliant with ICNIRP-1998 Reference Limit (6.25 μT), but approaching unipolar sensing threshold.
tiers.pacemaker_safety: Cardiac Caution: Legacy unipolar pacemakers with wide lead antenna loops may experience transient noise sensing.
tiers.clinical_verdict: Step back to 30 cm or switch to rear burner to restore safety margins.

tiers.name: Elevated EMF Radiation (Pacemaker EMI Risk Zone)
tiers.icnirp_compliance: Exceeds ICNIRP-1998 Public Guidance (6.25 μT); remains within ICNIRP-2010 ceiling (27 μT).
tiers.pacemaker_safety: Elevated Cardiac EMI Risk: Field can trigger asynchronous pacing mode (VOO/DOO) or inhibit pacing in sensitive leads.
tiers.clinical_verdict: Maintain minimum 40 cm separation distance immediately. Center cookware and avoid front edge contact.

tiers.name: Critical Stray Radiation (Severe EMI / Regulatory Non-Compliance)
tiers.icnirp_compliance: Exceeds ICNIRP-2010 Reference Level (27 μT) and violates IEC 62233 W<=1.0 ceiling.
tiers.pacemaker_safety: Critical EMI Hazard: Potential for inappropriate shock delivery in ICDs or total pacing suppression in pacemaker-dependent patients.
tiers.clinical_verdict: Decommission setup immediately. Pot is dangerously undersized or severely displaced from active coil.

faq_snippets.why_front_vs_rear: Cooking on rear burners adds approximately 25 to 30 cm of passive physical counter clearance from the user's torso. Because electromagnetic flux density decays exponentially (~1/r^2.5), this distance buffer attenuates stray magnetic fields by 85% to 95% before reaching a cardiac implant pocket.
faq_snippets.utensil_conductivity: Solid metal utensils (e.g., stainless steel spoons or wire whisks) held continuously in a pot during active induction cooking can couple with the alternating magnetic field, conducting small induced high-frequency currents into the cook's hand and forearm. Using wooden or heat-resistant silicone utensils completely eliminates this parasitic conduction path.
faq_snippets.icnirp_difference: ICNIRP 1998 set a conservative public reference limit of 6.25 μT for 20–100 kHz fields based on induced internal electric field thresholds in the central nervous system. In 2010, following updated micro-dosimetric modeling, ICNIRP raised the general public reference level to 27 μT. However, medical device manufacturers (e.g., Medtronic, Boston Scientific) still evaluate implant EMI immunity against conservative low-microtesla thresholds.
